---
title: "The Fleet Zoo"
subtitle: "Vetted Nodes, Racks, Fabrics, and Multi-Node Clusters"
---
The Fleet Zoo defines the **Structural Context** of ML systems—from single microcontrollers to
warehouse-scale supercomputers. Systems entries compose hardware nodes, rack profiles, network
fabrics, and cluster counts into complete structures that the `DistributedModel`, sustainability
models, and book LEGO cells can analyze.

::: {.callout-note}
## Understanding System Hierarchy
A **Fleet** = Node × Count + Fabric. The **Node** specifies which accelerator and how many per
server box. A **RackProfile** specifies a physical rack composition and power envelope. The
**Fabric** specifies how nodes talk to each other (NVLink for intra-node, InfiniBand for
inter-node). Use the [3D Parallelism tutorial](../tutorials/index.qmd) to see how these
parameters affect training time.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import mlsysim

_c_res = mlsysim.Systems.Clusters.Research_256
_c_1k = mlsysim.Systems.Clusters.Training_1K
_n_clusters = len(mlsysim.Systems.Clusters.list())
_bw_100g = mlsysim.Systems.Fabrics.Ethernet_100G.bandwidth.to("GB/s").magnitude
_bw_ndr = mlsysim.Systems.Fabrics.InfiniBand_NDR.bandwidth.to("GB/s").magnitude
_bw_ratio = _bw_ndr / _bw_100g

def print_node_table(title, node_class):
    print(f"### {title}")
    print("| Node Name | Accelerator | Count | Host CPU | Host Memory | Intra-Node BW |")
    print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|")
    for attr_name in sorted(dir(node_class)):
        if attr_name.startswith("_"): continue
        item = getattr(node_class, attr_name)
        if "Node" in type(item).__name__ and "HardwareNode" not in type(item).__name__:
            host_cpu = item.host_cpu if getattr(item, "host_cpu", None) is not None else "---"
            host_memory = f"{item.host_memory:~P}" if item.host_memory is not None else "---"
            print(f"| **{item.name}** | {item.accelerator.name} | {item.accelerators_per_node} | {host_cpu} | {host_memory} | {item.intra_node_bw:~P} |")
    print("\n")

def print_rack_table(title, rack_class):
    print(f"### {title}")
    print("| Rack Name | Node Type | Nodes | Accelerators | Accelerator Power | Support Power | Total Power |")
    print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|")
    for attr_name in sorted(dir(rack_class)):
        if attr_name.startswith("_"): continue
        item = getattr(rack_class, attr_name)
        if "RackProfile" in type(item).__name__:
            support_power = f"{item.non_accelerator_power:~P}" if item.non_accelerator_power is not None else "---"
            print(f"| **{item.name}** | {item.node.name} | {item.nodes_per_rack} | {item.accelerator_count} | {item.accelerator_power:~P} | {support_power} | {item.total_power:~P} |")
    print("\n")

def print_fabric_table(title, fabric_class):
    print(f"### {title}")
    print("| Fabric | Topology | Per-Port Bandwidth | Latency | Oversubscription |")
    print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|")
    for attr_name in sorted(dir(fabric_class)):
        if attr_name.startswith("_"): continue
        item = getattr(fabric_class, attr_name)
        if "NetworkFabric" in type(item).__name__:
            topo = getattr(item, "topology", None) or "---"
            bw = f"{item.bandwidth.to('GB/s'):~.1f}" if item.bandwidth is not None else "---"
            lat = f"{item.latency.to('us'):~.1f}" if item.latency is not None else "---"
            over = f"{item.oversubscription_ratio:g}:1" if getattr(item, "oversubscription_ratio", None) else "1:1"
            print(f"| **{item.name}** | {topo} | {bw} | {lat} | {over} |")
    print("\n")

def print_fleet_table(title, fleet_class):
    print(f"### {title}")
    print("| Cluster Name | Node Type | Node Count | Total GPUs | Fabric |")
    print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|")
    for attr_name in sorted(dir(fleet_class)):
        if attr_name.startswith("_"): continue
        item = getattr(fleet_class, attr_name)
        if "Fleet" in type(item).__name__:
            print(f"| **{item.name}** | {item.node.name} | {item.count} | {item.total_accelerators} | {item.fabric.name} |")
    print("\n")

def print_pod_table(title, pod_class):
    print(f"### {title}")
    print("| Pod Envelope | Chips | Total HBM | Power Envelope |")
    print("|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|")
    for attr_name in sorted(dir(pod_class)):
        if attr_name.startswith("_"): continue
        item = getattr(pod_class, attr_name)
        if "PodEnvelope" in type(item).__name__:
            mem = f"{item.memory.to('TB'):~.1f}" if item.memory is not None else "---"
            pwr = f"{item.power.to('MW'):~.2f}" if item.power is not None else "---"
            print(f"| **{item.name}** | {item.chips:,} | {mem} | {pwr} |")
    print("\n")

def print_storage_table(title, storage_class):
    print(f"### {title}")
    print("| Storage Subsystem | Media / Tech | Capacity | Sequential BW | Latency |")
    print("|:---|:---|:---:|:---:|:---:|")
    for attr_name in sorted(dir(storage_class)):
        if attr_name.startswith("_"): continue
        item = getattr(storage_class, attr_name)
        if "StorageSubsystem" in type(item).__name__:
            tech = getattr(item, "storage_tech", None) or getattr(item, "media", None) or "---"
            cap = f"{item.capacity:~P}" if item.capacity is not None else "---"
            bw = f"{item.bandwidth:~P}" if item.bandwidth is not None else "---"
            lat = f"{item.latency:~P}" if item.latency is not None else "---"
            print(f"| **{item.name}** | {tech} | {cap} | {bw} | {lat} |")
    print("\n")

reg = getattr(mlsysim, 'Systems', None)
if reg:
    if hasattr(reg, 'Nodes'): print_node_table("Reference Nodes", reg.Nodes)
    if hasattr(reg, 'Racks'): print_rack_table("Reference Racks", reg.Racks)
    if hasattr(reg, 'Fabrics'): print_fabric_table("Network Fabrics", reg.Fabrics)
    if hasattr(reg, 'Clusters'): print_fleet_table("Production Clusters", reg.Clusters)
    if hasattr(reg, 'Pods'): print_pod_table("TPU Pod Envelopes", reg.Pods)
    if hasattr(reg, 'Storage'): print_storage_table("Storage Subsystems", reg.Storage)
else:
    print("Error: Systems registry not found in mlsysim.")
```

## How to Read the Fleet Zoo

### Why Fleet Size Matters

Distributed training performance is dominated by **communication overhead** in large-scale systems such as DistBelief [@dean2012large]. As more nodes join, each all-reduce synchronization step must transfer gradient data across the fabric. The `DistributedModel` models this trade-off using the ring all-reduce cost model from Patarasuk and Yuan's bandwidth-optimal all-reduce analysis [-@patarasuk2009]:

$$T_{\text{dp}} = 2(N-1) \cdot \left(\frac{M/N}{BW} + L\right)$$

where $N$ is the GPU count, $M$ is the model size in bytes, and $BW$ is the fabric bandwidth.

### Rack Profiles Are System Facts

Rack profiles are composed system facts, not one-off arithmetic. A rack table may explain the
component breakdown, but the aggregate rack profile stays in `Systems.Racks.*` so every chapter
uses the same node count, accelerator count, support power, and total power.

### Why the Fabric Matters

Across the `{python} _n_clusters` registered cluster tiers, interconnect choice directly sets scaling efficiency. For example, `{python} _c_res.name` pairs `{python} _c_res.node.name` servers over 100 GbE (`{python} f"{_bw_100g:.1f} GB/s"` per link), whereas `{python} _c_1k.name` pairs `{python} _c_1k.node.name` servers over InfiniBand NDR (`{python} f"{_bw_ndr:.0f} GB/s"` per link, a `{python} f"{_bw_ratio:.0f}×"` per-port step-up across `{python} _c_1k.node.nics_per_node` NICs per node). Try both in the [Scaling to 1000 GPUs tutorial](../tutorials/06_scaling_1000_gpus.qmd) to see how collective communication latency shifts.

### Deployment Envelopes (`Platforms`)

Abstract deployment envelopes (Cloud, Edge, Mobile, TinyML RAM/storage/latency ranges, formerly `Systems.Tiers`) now live in their own registry: see the [Platforms Zoo](platforms.qmd).
